PHASE_0_ENVIRONMENT: Modal CPU only -- no gpu= appears anywhere in scratchpad/modal_partition.py or its high-memory variant scratchpad/modal_partition_hi.py; both are scanned by _l1ov_cost.py
KAHIP_BUILD_NOTE: debian_slim lacks MPI; KaHIP's CMakeLists calls find_package(MPI) unconditionally, so without libopenmpi-dev no Makefile is generated and deploy/ holds only the header.  -march=native additionally produced a binary that SIGILLs (rc -4) because Modal builds and runs on different CPUs.
IMBALANCE_NOTE: production pymetis used ufactor=30, which in METIS means 1+30/1000 = 3%, NOT 30%.  Measured production max/mean is 1.025-1.030, confirming 3%.  KaHIP --imbalance and Mt-KaHyPar epsilon are given the same 3%.
IMAGE_CACHED: KaHIP compiled once into the image layer; never rebuilt per corpus
MEMORY_REQUEST_NOTE: HotpotQA was first re-tried in a 192 GB container on the hypothesis that the 64 GB one had been OOM-killed.  That hypothesis is REFUTED by measurement: HotpotQA H3_MTKAHYPAR_GRAPH:G1_LOCAL_HYPER_CLIQUE completed inside the 64 GB container at 833 s with a peak RSS of 41.4 GB, and the largest peak seen anywhere is 43.8 GB (WebQSP).  Memory was never the binding constraint; the larger request is kept only as headroom and changes no partition.
HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_CAUSE: the real cause of the repeated HotpotQA failures is the GIL, not memory.  mtkahypar's Python binding holds the GIL for the whole of hg.partition(ctx), and the graph/hyperedge construction above it is a multi-million-iteration pure-Python loop that holds it too, so on a >900 s call Modal's runner-heartbeat thread never gets scheduled and the task is killed as unresponsive.  The KaHIP path never failed despite a 2389 s partition because it goes through subprocess.run, which releases the GIL.  Fix: modal_partition_hi.py runs Mt-KaHyPar in a child process (same binary, preset, seed and epsilon), so the parent stays responsive.  This is a runner-plumbing change only -- it cannot alter a partition.
